questions.q: State the formula for heat produced by an electric current in a resistor and name the SI unit of each quantity.
questions.a: The formula is H = I²Rt. H (heat) is measured in joules (J), I (current) in amperes (A), R (resistance) in ohms (Ω), and t (time) in seconds (s). A wrong answer such as H = I R t (missing the square on current) reveals the student does not recall the quadratic dependence on current, which is the most distinctive feature of Joule's law.

questions.q: Why does doubling the current through a resistor quadruple the heat produced, while doubling the resistance only doubles the heat (assuming current stays constant)? Explain using the formula H = I²Rt.
questions.a: In H = I²Rt, current (I) is squared, so if I becomes 2I, the I² term becomes (2I)² = 4I², multiplying heat by 4. Resistance (R) is to the first power, so doubling R only doubles H. A wrong answer that says "both double the heat" shows the student treats the formula as linear in all variables and misses the physical reason: heat depends on the *rate* of energy transfer (power = I²R), and power itself depends on I².

questions.q: An electric iron draws a current of 4 A from a 220 V supply. Its heating element has a resistance of 55 Ω. Calculate the heat produced in joules if the iron is used for 2 minutes.
questions.a: Given: I = 4 A, R = 55 Ω, t = 2 min = 120 s. Formula: H = I²Rt = (4)² × 55 × 120 = 16 × 55 × 120 = 105,600 J. Unit analysis: A² × Ω × s = (C/s)² × (J·s/C²) × s = J. A wrong answer of 26,400 J (using H = I R t) reveals the student forgot to square the current. A wrong answer of 1,760 J (using t = 2 s instead of 120 s) reveals a unit conversion error.

questions.q: Two identical resistors are connected (a) in series and (b) in parallel across the same battery. In which case is more heat produced per minute? Explain using H = I²Rt and the equivalent resistance.
questions.a: More heat is produced in the parallel combination. For the same voltage, the equivalent resistance in parallel (R/2) is lower than in series (2R). The total current drawn from the battery is higher in parallel (I_parallel = V/(R/2) = 2V/R) than in series (I_series = V/(2R)). Since total heat H = I²R_eq t, for parallel: H_parallel = (2V/R)² × (R/2) × t = (4V²/R²) × (R/2) × t = 2V²t/R. For series: H_series = (V/(2R))² × (2R) × t = (V²/4R²) × 2R × t = 0.5 V²t/R. Parallel produces 4 times more heat. A wrong answer choosing series reveals the student thinks "higher resistance always means more heat" without considering that the current changes drastically when the circuit configuration changes.

questions.q: A student calculates the heat produced in a 10 Ω resistor carrying 2 A for 30 s as H = 2 × 10 × 30 = 600 J. Evaluate this solution and identify the error.
questions.a: The solution is incorrect. The student used H = I R t instead of H = I² R t. The correct calculation is H = (2)² × 10 × 30 = 4 × 10 × 30 = 1,200 J. The error is omitting the square on the current. This reveals a fundamental misunderstanding of the formula: the student treats heat as linearly proportional to current, whereas the physics (Joule's law) shows a quadratic relationship because power = I²R.

questions.q: Design a simple experiment using a battery, a variable resistor (rheostat), an ammeter, a calorimeter with water, and a thermometer to verify that heat produced is proportional to the square of the current (H ∝ I²). List the steps and the graph you would plot.
questions.a: Steps: (1) Set up a circuit with battery, rheostat, ammeter, and a heating coil immersed in a known mass of water in a calorimeter. (2) Adjust rheostat to get a current I₁, close circuit for fixed time t, measure temperature rise Δθ₁. Calculate H₁ = mcΔθ₁. (3) Repeat for at least 4 different currents I₂, I₃... keeping time and water mass constant. (4) Plot H (y-axis) vs I² (x-axis). A straight line through origin verifies H ∝ I². A poor answer that plots H vs I (getting a curve) or does not control time/mass reveals the student cannot isolate variables or translate a proportionality into a graphical test.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The heat energy produced when an electric current passes through a resistor is given by Joule's law of heating: H = I²Rt, where H is the heat energy in joules (J), I is the current in amperes (A), R is the ______ in ohms (Ω), and t is the time in seconds (s).
Fill in the blank: Observe an electric room heater or a geyser in an Indian ______: the element glows red and the room warms up.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can calculate the heat produced in a resistor given any three of the four quantities (H, I, R, t) and can predict qualitatively how the heat changes if one factor is altered while others are kept constant, using the correct proportionality relationships.
